extracted.intended_audience: applicants, practitioners, and USPTO personnel involved in filing or processing international design (Hague) applications (including attorneys, agents, and examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for preparing and filing international design (Hague) applications, including required/optional contents, reproductions (drawings/photographs), form DM/1 usage, annexes, and fee/payment rules, with special rules when the United States is designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of an international design application
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory contents (Article 5(1), Rule 7, 37 CFR 1.1021(a)): application must be in English, French, or Spanish; presented on the official form; signed by the applicant; and must include: (1) a request for Hague registration; (2) prescribed data concerning the applicant; (3) the prescribed number of copies of a reproduction or, at applicant's choice, several different reproductions of the industrial design presented in the prescribed manner (or specimens where allowed); (4) an indication of the product(s) that constitute the industrial design or in relation to which it is to be used; (5) indication of designated Contracting Parties; (6) the prescribed fees; (7) the Contracting Party(ies) for which the applicant fulfills conditions to be the holder; (8) the number of industrial designs included (may not exceed 100) and number of reproductions/specimens; (9) the amount of fees being paid and method of payment or instructions to debit an IB account and identification of the party effecting payment; and (10) an indication of applicant's Contracting Party as required under Rule 7(4)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are mandatory in all international design applications; use of the official form DM/1 helps ensure inclusion of these items. See MPEP § 2909.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional mandatory contents (where required by designated Contracting Parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements required by certain Contracting Parties (Article 5(2), Rule 7, 37 CFR 1.1021(b)) may include: indications concerning the identity of the creator; a brief description of the reproduction or of the characteristic features of the industrial design; and/or a claim; and pursuant to Rule 8(1), a statement, document, oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory only when a designated Contracting Party requires them; applicants should include them when designating such Contracting Parties to avoid defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional contents of an international design application
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional contents (Rule 7(5), 37 CFR 1.1021(c)) may include: (1) two or more industrial designs subject to prescribed conditions; (2) a request for deferment of publication or immediate publication; (3) any additional mandatory elements even if not required by any designated Contracting Party; (4) prescribed information concerning applicant’s representative; (5) a claim of priority of earlier applications (may be accompanied by a DAS access code); (6) a declaration for Article 11 Paris Convention exhibition; (7) any declaration/statement as specified in Administrative Instructions; (8) a statement identifying information known by applicant to be material to eligibility; and (9) a proposed translation of text matter for recording/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of optional contents can be strategic (e.g., priority claims, translations) but must comply with prescribed formats and possible additional fees (e.g., description exceeding 100 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim requirement when the United States is designated
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States must contain a claim (37 CFR 1.1021(d); U.S. declared under Article 5(2)). The claim is a filing date requirement for design applications in the U.S. (35 U.S.C. 171).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application designating the U.S. lacks a claim, the International Bureau will invite submission of the claim within a prescribed time; failure to timely submit will result in the application being deemed not to contain the designation of the United States (no U.S. filing date). Using official form DM/1 (which includes a claim field) helps ensure compliance. See MPEP §§ 2903, 2907, 2908, 2909.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator identity and inventor's oath/declaration when the United States is designated
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Rule 11(1) and Rule 8(1) as declared by the U.S., an international design application designating the United States must contain indications concerning the identity of the creator and an inventor's oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.1021(d); 37 CFR 1.63 and 1.64).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements to identify each inventor by legal name, mailing address, and residence (and related substitute-statement requirements) are considered satisfied by presentation of such information in the international application prior to international registration. If the oath/declaration is not filed, the IB will invite submission; failure to timely submit will result in the application being deemed not to contain the U.S. designation. Annex I to DM/1 provides inventor’s oath and substitute-statement forms for U.S. designation. See MPEP § 2909.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and brief description requirement for U.S. designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 and preferably include a brief description of the reproductions pursuant to Rule 7(5)(a) (37 CFR 1.1024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO encourages inclusion of a brief description of the view(s) of the reproductions (helpful for examination and scope/disclosure issues). Such brief descriptions should be placed in Item (10) 'Legends (optional)' of form DM/1. A description may be required in a nonprovisional international design application under 37 CFR 1.1067. See MPEP § 2920.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on deferment of publication and specimens for U.S. designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States may not contain a request for deferment of publication (37 CFR 1.1028). Specimens are not permitted in applications designating the United States (37 CFR 1.1027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants designating the U.S. must not request deferred publication and must file reproductions (not specimens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official form (DM/1) and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The international design application shall be presented on the official form (DM/1) (Hague Rule 7(1) and Rule 1(vi)) and shall be signed by the applicant (37 CFR 1.1022). 'Official form' means the form established by the International Bureau or an electronic interface with the same contents/format (eHague).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper use of the DM/1 form helps ensure mandatory, additional mandatory, and optional items are present. DM/1 and eHague instructions are available on WIPO’s website. The form contains specific spaces for numerous required items (see separate DM/1 contents entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: DM/1 form content fields (what DM/1 includes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form DM/1 includes specific spaces to set forth: (1) information concerning the applicant; (2) applicant’s entitlement to file; (3) correspondence address for the IB where multiple applicants and no appointed representative; (4) appointment of a representative; (5) industrial designs and reproductions included; (6) designated Contracting Parties; (7) applicable product and Locarno classification; (8) number of reproductions; (9) a description; (10) a description of the reproductions; (11) identity of the creator; (12) a claim; (13) priority claim; (14) information regarding any international exhibition where designs were shown; (15) exception to lack of novelty; (16) relation with a principal design; (17) request for immediate or deferred publication; (18) reduction of individual designation fee; (19) signature of applicant or representative; and a Payment of Fees section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filling the DM/1 fields as intended reduces the risk of defects and missing mandatory items. Annexes I–V are available for particular Contracting Party-specific submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions must comply with Hague Rule 9 and Administrative Instructions Part Four
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions (drawings/photographs) shall comply with Rule 9 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions (37 CFR 1.1026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following detailed reproduction requirements are derived from Rule 9 and Administrative Instructions (Sections 401–405) and must be followed to avoid refusals for insufficient disclosure or form defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and number of reproductions (Rule 9(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions may be photographs or other graphic representations of the industrial design itself or of the product(s) which constitute the industrial design; the same product may be shown from different angles, and views from different angles shall be included in different photographs/representations. The number of copies must be as specified in the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each view should be a separate reproduction (file). Administrative Instructions specify number of copies and layout rules (see Section 401).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and disclosure sufficiency of reproductions (Rule 9(2) and Rule 9(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions shall be of a quality permitting all the details of the industrial design to be clearly distinguished and permitting publication. A Contracting Party may refuse the effects of the international registration if the reproductions in the international registration are not sufficient to disclose fully the industrial design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To minimize refusal risk, follow IB guidance 'Guidance on Preparing and Providing Reproductions' (available on WIPO website) and Administrative Instructions. Matter shown but not claimed may be indicated as provided in Admin. Instr.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views required and view limits (Rule 9(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting Party bound by the 1999 Act may notify required specified views and the circumstances in which they are required. No Contracting Party may require more than one view where the design/product is two-dimensional, or more than six views where the product is three-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Guide to the Hague System for Contracting Party-specific view requirements. Provide required views to avoid objections from designated offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation rules for reproductions (Administrative Instructions Section 401)
rubrics_metrics.description: One and the same international application may comprise photographs and other graphic representations; each reproduction accompanying an application shall be submitted in a single copy; photographs/graphic representations filed on paper must be pasted or printed onto a separate A4 sheet (white and opaque), used upright, with no more than 25 reproductions per sheet; reproductions must be arranged in publication orientation; a margin of at least 5 mm should be left around each representation; each reproduction must fall within a right-angled quadrilateral containing no other reproduction or part thereof and no numbering; representations shall not be folded, stapled, or marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these physical presentation rules for paper filings; electronic filing formats may be specified by the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation content rules (Administrative Instructions Section 402)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs and graphic representations shall represent the industrial design alone, or the product in relation to which it is to be used, to the exclusion of any other object, accessory, person or animal. Dimensions of each representation may not exceed 16 x 16 centimeters, and at least one representation of each design must have one dimension of at least 3 centimeters. The following shall not be accepted in representations: (i) technical drawings, particularly with axes and dimensions; (ii) explanatory text or legends in the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reproductions focus only on the design/product, meet size limits, and avoid technical drawings or embedded explanatory text/legends; for electronic filing check IB-specified data formats to ensure compliance with size limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating matter not forming part of the design (Administrative Instructions Section 403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter shown in a reproduction but for which protection is not sought may be indicated either in the description referred to in Rule 7(5)(a) and/or by means of dotted or broken lines or coloring. Matter not forming part of the industrial design or product may be shown if indicated in accordance with paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dotted/broken lines or coloring or the description to disclaim elements not claimed, per Admin. Instr. 403, to clarify scope of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and graphic representation quality requirements (Administrative Instructions Section 404)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs must be of professional standard with all edges cut at right angles; design shown against a neutral plain background; photographs retouched with ink or correcting fluid are not allowed. Graphic representations must be of professional standard, produced with drawing instruments or electronic means, and where filed on paper produced on good quality white, opaque paper with edges cut at right angles; shading and hatching to provide relief are allowed; electronic graphic representations may be shown against a neutral plain background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure high professional quality for both photos and graphic representations and avoid any retouching that alters the image; adherence reduces risk of publication/examination objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of reproductions and legends (Administrative Instructions Section 405)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbering for multiple international applications shall appear in the margin of each reproduction; when the same design is represented from different angles, numbering shall consist of two separate figures separated by a dot (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3). Reproductions shall be submitted in ascending numerical order. Legends to indicate a specific view (e.g., 'front view') may be indicated in association with the numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prescribed numbering conventions and submit files in ascending order; include legends where helpful to identify views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Annexes to DM/1 for Contracting Party-specific items
rubrics_metrics.description: Annexes to DM/1 (Annexes I–V) provide required or optional items relevant to particular designated Contracting Parties and are available on WIPO’s website. Annexes specific to the U.S. include Annex I (inventor’s oath/declaration), Annex III (information disclosure statement), and Annex IV (certification of micro entity status). Annex II and V are specific to other designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate annexes when designating Contracting Parties that require/allow specific supplemental documents or statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design application fees: transmittal fee (USPTO filing as office of indirect filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: International design applications filed through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing are subject to a transmittal fee (35 U.S.C. 382(b), 37 CFR 1.1031(a)). Current amounts: micro entity $24.00; small entity $48.00; other than small/micro $120.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal fee must be paid in U.S. dollars through the USPTO; the USPTO will not transmit the application to the International Bureau if the transmittal fee is not paid. Payment timing is important to preserve filing date benefits (see timing entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau fees, schedule, and payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Hague Rule 12, international applications are subject to payment of a basic fee, standard or individual designation fees, and a publication fee; an additional word fee applies where the description exceeds 100 words. International Bureau fees may be paid directly to the IB in Swiss currency or through the Office (via USPTO) in U.S. dollars, subject to timing and possible currency-conversion shortfalls requiring additional payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The WIPO Hague System Fee Calculator (on WIPO website) helps determine amounts; fees payable to the IB may also include renewal fees (submitted directly to IB). Applicants paying fees through the USPTO may be subject to additional amounts where currency conversion results in the IB receiving less than prescribed amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation fee structure for the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: The designation fee for the United States consists of two parts: (1) a first part established in Swiss currency pursuant to Hague Rule 28 based on combined amounts of basic filing, search, and examination fees for a design application (payable at filing); and (2) a second part (issue fee) as provided in 37 CFR 1.18(b) payable within the period specified in a notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect a two-part fee for U.S. designation and pay the first part at filing (in Swiss currency to the IB or through proper channels). The second part is paid later per notice of allowance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: When fees must be paid and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees referred to in Rule 12 are payable at the time of filing the international application, except where a request for deferment of publication is made and the publication fee may be paid later. For applications filed via USPTO as office of indirect filing, fees payable to the IB must be paid no later than the date of payment of the transmittal fee. If an international design application is not received by the International Bureau within six months from the date it is received by the USPTO, it will not be entitled to a filing date as of the date of receipt by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment and transmission to the IB are critical to secure international filing dates and avoid loss of designation or priority benefits. See Hague Rule 13 and 37 CFR 1.1045.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of reproductions via USPTO patent electronic filing system
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions may be submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system as single-page PDF or JPEG files attached using the 'Reproductions' section (or as PDFs via 'Upload documents'). Each image file attached through the 'Reproductions' section should contain only one view; the system assigns design and view numbers to files. The system will not permit submission of a 'Reproductions' file exceeding two megabytes (JPEG) and will not permit multi-page PDF files via the 'Reproductions' section. The system provides warnings about resolution, dimensions, and possible per-page publication fees but does not fully check color mode, border size, or all resolution parameters for all file types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are responsible for ensuring reproductions meet all IB technical and Administrative Instructions requirements prior to upload; attaching via 'Reproductions' rather than general 'Upload documents' may avoid additional per-page publication fees.
